environment.element_sas: not exercised; requires a human client action
environment.openrig_transport: tools/fake_openrig.py subprocess protocol; not live Codex

known_gaps: Real Codex prompt delivery and native transcript completion are represented by the fake OpenRig subprocess transport.
The Parakeet model and real voice transcription were not run.
Element device-to-device SAS verification was not run.
Federation, public homeserver policy, and production E2EE device trust were not exercised.

redaction.access_tokens: not written to the report or bridge log
redaction.ephemeral_state: removed after the run unless --keep-workdir is set

results.evidence: Started disposable Synapse matrixdotorg/synapse@sha256:390f5e67227378eb87c84627b57f0582cdb235fcc8159d89f371f37bf7cccfd7 on loopback; the container and state directory are removed at exit unless `--keep-workdir` is set.
`setup` wrote one agent room; `doctor` exited 0 (wrote /tmp/openrig-matrix-integration.6r5at_5r/config.yaml with 1 agent room(s))

Synapse accepted the owner invite and join; the room uses `m.megolm.v1.aes-sha2`, has a managed room avatar, exposes a downloadable Relay bridge-account profile avatar with identical bytes, and publishes ready topic plus `dev.openrig.agent_status` state.

Owner text was encrypted by matrix-nio; the fake OpenRig subprocess received it exactly once, and the recorded qitem history is pending -> in-progress -> done. Typing was observed, commentary was mirrored in one activity-labelled card, and the final answer returned separately in-thread. The raw thread relation references the owner prompt. The homeserver API reported the final event as raw `m.room.encrypted` with Megolm ciphertext.

An encrypted owner prompt already in m.thread survived a bridge restart while the fake seat was busy. Commentary and final answer were each delivered once under the canonical thread root, and the single Matrix qitem completed pending -> in-progress -> done.
The bridge exited immediately after claiming an OpenRig qitem. Restart recognized the in-progress qitem, resumed the unsent prompt exactly once, and completed the same qitem.
The bridge process exited immediately after the final Matrix answer send. Restart retried with the persisted transaction ID, Matrix deduplicated to the same event, and the single qitem completed.

A second owner message arrived during a deliberately slow first turn; Matrix showed the pinned queue notice and the fake OpenRig transport received the second prompt only after recording completion of the first (1792879539.8550303 < 1792879540.3983533).

Disposable-Synapse probes verified queue mode remains FIFO, steer mode injects one ordered two-event same-thread batch under its canonical root, and auto mode steers only the short same-thread follow-up while top-level and other-thread requests advance FIFO. All source qitems closed, and an unrelated human transcript turn did not steal the Matrix answer.

With the fake transport refusing busy injection, the complete two-message batch remained durably queued and was sent once as one normal fallback turn. A process crash immediately after successful pane injection recovered from transcript admission without resending the batch.
Owner reaction reached the fake OpenRig transport as silent feedback and did not create a visible bot reply.
Owner PNG was decrypted, signature-checked, stored byte-for-byte, and forwarded; `send-image` produced an encrypted Matrix image that the owner client downloaded and decrypted byte-for-byte.

Encrypted PDF and unknown binary attachments were transferred in both directions through disposable Synapse, and markerless audio used the generic attachment path. Inbound files were stored under generated agent inbox paths with original metadata; outbound m.file events used private snapshots with preserved filename, MIME type and size, decrypted byte-for-byte, and were Megolm-encrypted on the wire.

A generic-file request was durably queued while the bridge was stopped, then delivered exactly once after restart. The persisted success record names the same Matrix event ID observed by the owner; the delivered bytes came from the private snapshot even after the mutable source was replaced.

A PDF and markerless audio sent from inside an existing m.thread were stored and forwarded. Every file status and final bridge message used the original canonical thread root, and each input created one completed qitem.

An encrypted Matrix audio event reached the bridge and received the configured disabled-voice response after a controlled configuration restart. Real Parakeet quality remains an explicit gap; the successful voice path uses a deterministic local transcriber.

A deterministic transcriber produced one local transcript for an encrypted voice note. Matrix showed one threaded progress event edited in place by `m.replace`; no transcript-only reply was sent. The prompt and single qitem each completed exactly once. Real Parakeet execution and Element rendering remain explicit gaps.
Decision brief and MSC3381 poll were published and pinned; an encrypted poll response was returned to the fake transport as a decision prompt and the decision events were unpinned.
`send-message` delivered an encrypted proactive message to the owner.
Stopping and restarting the bridge preserved the exact Matrix room mapping and returned the room to ready status without creating a duplicate room.
`doctor` exited non-zero and reported the invalid Matrix token.
Owner leave was detected, the bridge left the room, persisted a rejection tombstone, and a restart did not recreate it.
